| Scene description | • The site is near Simenkou & Yellow Crane Tower Metro Station.<br>• S10-B-03: a worn red plastic box on gray paving beside stainless-steel barriers is recognized as accumulation, without other obvious waste.<br>• S10-B-04: two clean gray sorting-bin sets below an entrance slope bear M Hongqiang Alley REDWOW! branding, without spillage, before colorful graffiti.<br>• S10-B-05: three stained black wheeled bins stand near small-goods stalls and pedestrians. The central and right bins are recognized as overflowing above their rims; the left does not overflow. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be clean, spill-free, and accessible without obstructing passage. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 32.<br>• Casual public stockpiling or dumping is prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 29.<br>• Overflow requires prompt collection against secondary pollution or appearance impacts. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 15.<br>• Station managers should maintain sanitation and functioning collection facilities. Provisions on Urban Rail Transit Operations Management, Article 31.<br>• Organizations or individuals failing duties or causing sanitation problems through unremoved overflow or accumulation may receive warnings or fines. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two overflowing bins and one accumulation affect a busy station area, impairing appearance and posing sanitation risks without extensive pollution or serious harm. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: overflow exposes waste; retained accumulations may cause insects or odors. Possible short-term impacts: heavy pedestrian use may prompt complaints and reputational harm, while rain may spread waste onto ground or drains. |
| Potential causes | - Concentrated stall activity and pedestrians at S10-B-05 may generate more waste than collections handle.<br>- The nonstandard red box at S10-B-03 may be improper temporary business or personal storage or missed removal.<br>- Verify collections, provision and maintenance inventories, and collection-vehicle frequency against generation. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, neglected accumulations may breed insects and bacteria affecting health, undermine trust in urban management, and increase enforcement and cleaning costs. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** empty S10-B-05, clear S10-B-03, disinfect bins, and remove or properly manage the nonstandard red box.<br>- **Long-term measures:** increase peak collections, provide temporary bins or scheduled stall collections, educate businesses and users, inspect regularly, and establish feedback. |
| Priority | **Medium.** No severe pollution or safety harm occurs, but overflow and accumulation in a busy station setting impair appearance and public experience and pose sanitation risks. Short-term action should prevent escalation. |
